$comment: Canonical feature map of the v12 restructure (artifacts/restructure-plan/PLAN.md, 'Canonical feature list'). One row per feature, plus the two areas that are not features (admin, platform).
client: repo-relative client/src folders. For a feature the first one is client/src/features/<name>.
backend: the folder under backendRoot (backend.md §7.4: feature folders = this column; there is no kebab-to-Pascal rule). null = no backend folder; backendServedBy names the folder that serves it.
controller: the feature's controller type (Je<Feature>Controller, partials Je<Feature>Controller.<Area>.cs allowed); null = none.

tests.frontend / tests.backend: repo-relative test folders. Step F1 mirrored feature tests into tests/frontend/features/<name> where they had a by-prefix home; the rest stay in the cross-cutting folders F1 kept (bootstrap, core, pages, requests, chrome), which a row then names.

tests.backend names only the feature's own tests/backend/Features/<backend> folder (FeatureMapParityTests.BackendTestFoldersMatchTheMap rejects another feature's folder). A feature whose backend tests sit in other folders' mixed files lists none, and its notes say where they are.

Read by tests/frontend/architecture/feature-map.test.mjs and feature-readme.test.mjs (frontend), tests/backend/Architecture/FeatureMapParityTests.cs (backend) and the CONTRIBUTING.md 'Where things live' table. admin-tags is folded into media-tags on both sides.

features.name: activity
features.notes: Its frontend tests (pages-activity, pages-social-*, pages-plugin-pages-features) stay in the cross-cutting pages/ folder, which F1 kept. Backend: tests/backend/Features/Activity holds the ActivityFeedBuilder tests (round 13 moved them out of DetailsProviders/ReviewActivityVisibilityTests.cs). The activity store itself is Configuration/UserConfigurationManager, tested in tests/backend/Core/CoreSharedStoresTests.cs.

features.name: calendar
features.notes: Its frontend tests (pages-calendar*) stay in the cross-cutting pages/ folder, which F1 kept.

features.name: catchup
features.notes: Its frontend tests (pages-social-*) stay in the cross-cutting pages/ folder, which F1 kept. Backend: no tests/backend/Features/Catchup folder; JeCatchupController is covered only by tests/backend/Architecture/ControllerActivationTests.cs and the route/auth snapshots.

features.name: chrome
features.notes: Branding, active streams. Its frontend tests already have their own folder, which F1 keeps.

features.name: downloads
features.notes: Backend: tests/backend/Features/Downloads holds the arr/queue, arr/history and arr/requests route tests (round 13 moved them out of Seerr/ApiSeerrTests.cs; they still use its Seerr fixture).

features.name: hidden-content
features.notes: Its settings-panel section is in settings/.

features.name: media-tags
features.notes: Was admin-tags / AdminTags. The admin page is in admin/ and the settings-panel sections in settings/; the admin routes are in JeMediaTagsController.Admin.cs.

features.name: seerr
features.notes: Its frontend tests stay in the cross-cutting requests/ and pages/ (pages-seerr-*, -moreinfo, -scroll, -discovery*, -recommendations*) folders, which F1 kept.

features.name: settings
features.notes: Its frontend tests (settings-revisions, bootstrap, bootstrap-loader-rewrite) stay in the cross-cutting bootstrap/ folder, which F1 kept.

features.name: settings-panel
features.notes: The panel shell; feature sections live in their features.

features.name: shared
features.notes: Pure helpers every feature may import. Part of Platform; not the backend Shared/ layer. Its frontend tests (core-shared-*, core-translat*) stay in the cross-cutting core/ folder, which F1 kept.

features.name: admin
features.notes: The plugin configuration page. Not under features/.

features.name: platform
features.notes: Bootstrap, core services and hosts. The backend Shared/ and Infrastructure/ folders are layers, not features.
